行政長官李家超今到立法會參與首場「對談交流會」，會後與立法會主席李慧琼會見傳媒。李家超回應宏福苑長遠居住安排時，指已有 53% 業主簽訂買賣協議，籲住戶「把握時間作決定」。他另回應陳嘉信涉司法抄襲被提早退休事件，指尊重首席法官採適當措施，維護公眾對法官獨立專業履責的信心。至於黃錦輝涉醉駕請辭而空缺的議席，會否進行補選，李家超指未來 18 個月有三場重要選舉，認為在時間、工作、相對必要性方面，應先做好這三場選舉。

Chief Executive John Lee today attended the "Dialogue Exchange" at the Legislative Council and answered media questions afterward.

53% of owners have signed sale agreements; nearly 91% have signed acquisition acceptance letters

Asked about the progress of the Wang Fuk Court acquisition and whether the reasons of residents who have not yet signed consent forms had been looked into, Lee said the Wang Fuk Court matter has always been handled with "compassion, reason, and the law." He reiterated that, regarding long-term housing arrangements, the Government is acquiring the property titles at a rate of HK$8,000 to HK$10,500 per square foot, and is bearing various risks, including the uncertainty of insurance compensation and the potential risks of different legal proceedings.

He said that as of yesterday, 90.8% of owners had signed the letter accepting the acquisition proposal and 53% had completed the sale and purchase agreement, with owners also gradually completing the formal assignment of titles. He described the process as smooth and said, "I hope everyone will seize the time to make a decision." He also pointed out that the decision is, of course, for each household to make after weighing their actual circumstances. As for the acquisition price, risk-bearing, and the provision of other assistance, "the hope is to allow the affected households to make a decision as soon as possible, so that everyone can return to normal life at an early date." He also noted that units will soon be released for residents to consider, saying: "If you seize this opportunity early, you may be able to apply for the long-term residence unit of your choice."

Lee again reiterated that the Government has recently optimised the rental subsidy arrangements and that the Legislative Council's application for an allocation of HK$1 billion to acquire Wang Tsz Court has also been approved. The Government will continue to do a good job of explanation, and households with questions or requests may relay them to the explanation team or the one-household-one-social-worker scheme. They will be handled flexibly and pragmatically according to the actual circumstances.

Asked about the long-term housing arrangements for Wang Fuk Court, Lee said 53% of owners have signed the sale and purchase agreement, with some owners having completed the assignment of titles. He described the process as smooth.

Responding to the early retirement of judge Jonathan Man following plagiarism allegations: respecting the Chief Justice's appropriate measures

As for the Court of First Instance judge Jonathan Man, who was found to have plagiarised on multiple occasions and was required by Chief Justice Andrew Cheung to retire early yesterday, Lee was asked whether this was sufficient to restore public confidence. Lee said society holds high expectations for judges and their professional standards, and the Judiciary has always operated and been managed independently. He said he respects the Chief Justice's adoption of appropriate measures to uphold public confidence in the independent and professional fulfilment of duties by judges, and he is confident that judges and judicial officers at all levels will abide by the judicial oath and discharge their judicial duties with diligence, independence, and professionalism.

High Court judge Jonathan Man, who was involved in a plagiarism scandal, has been required to take early retirement. The Chief Executive responded today, saying he respects the Chief Justice's appropriate measures to maintain public confidence. (File photo)

Separately, University of Hong Kong (HKU) President Xiang Zhang, who was previously embroiled in a school governance controversy, said yesterday that he would step down after completing two terms totalling 10 years in 2028. Asked for his assessment and whether he would require HKU to include terms requiring good communication with the Council when hiring a new president, Lee said that Zhang, as a scientist who loves science, is eager to return to the laboratory to solve scientific problems and contribute to society. He thanked Zhang for notifying the University Council of his decision in advance, giving the University sufficient time to recruit a new president.

Lee also thanked Zhang for his hard work and contributions to HKU during his past and future tenure as president. He said the work of recruiting a president would be handled by the University Council, noting that universities have well-functioning mechanisms for hiring presidents. He expressed confidence in the Council handling the work well and believed it would ensure that the new president leads HKU to continue developing and making progress.

HKU President Xiang Zhang announced yesterday that he will step down in 2028. Lee expressed gratitude for his contributions to HKU and expressed confidence that the University Council will handle the recruitment well. (File photo)

No by-election for time being following Andy Wong's resignation: priority is to hold the next three elections well

Legislative Council member Andy Wong was arrested for drunk driving at the end of last month and resigned from his position earlier this month. The outside world is paying attention to whether a by-election will be held. Secretary for Constitutional and Mainland Affairs Alice Mak had earlier indicated that the timing was relatively tight. Asked about the by-election again today, Lee said that three important elections will be held in the next 18 months, including the Election Committee election in November this year, the Chief Executive election in March next year, and the District Council election before the end of next year. He said that for any election, the Electoral Affairs Commission (EAC) would consider a range of factors, including human resources, venue arrangements, polling station setup, and the procurement and transportation of election supplies. It must consider the overall work arrangements and the relative necessity of each election according to the actual circumstances.

Lee added that after the Election Committee election is completed in November this year, it will take office on 1 February next year to perform its role in the relevant elections. He believed that, compared with a single Legislative Council by-election, "in terms of time, workload, and relative necessity, these three elections should be prioritised."

Wong resigned after being involved in a drunk driving incident, and all sectors are concerned about whether a by-election will be held for the vacant seat. Lee said priority should be given to ensuring the smooth conduct of the next three elections, while Legislative Council President Starry Lee said she respects the assessment of the Chief Executive and the EAC.

Asked whether the reduction in the number of members would affect the work of the Legislative Council and whether she had discussed the matter with Xia Baolong, Starry Lee said she understands and respects the assessment of the Chief Executive and the EAC. She said that as an important working partner of the Government, the Legislative Council will certainly cooperate with and support the proper delivery of a series of important tasks first, including the first five-year plan and the policy address. She continued that although there have been changes in the Legislative Council, which now has only 89 members, "I believe every member will understand that they need to take one more step, support each other more, and share the burden together in response to the new situation caused by unpredictable changes." She said all members will go all out, and with the joint efforts of 89 members, the functions of the entire Council will be delivered as always.

No response on whether the Huanggang Port will commence operation before 1 October

The relevant bill for the Hong Kong port area of the new Huanggang Port was passed by the Legislative Council earlier, and together with the relevant subsidiary legislation, will come into effect on 31 July. However, the date for the opening of the border crossing has not yet been announced. Asked whether the port could officially open before 1 October, Lee did not give a direct response, saying he understood that everyone was very concerned about the port. He noted that after the Hong Kong port area is established on 31 July, the governments of Hong Kong and Shenzhen will conduct operational tests on the port's operations, including systems, installations, and traffic stress testing. He stressed that the installation, facilities, testing and drills for the port are being pushed forward at full speed, with the goal of completing them as soon as possible and opening the port to the public at an early date. He said a decision would be announced when made.
